Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). The owner reviewed a live screenshot of the mod card (used across `/mods`, `/mods/games/[family]`, `/dashboard/nxlabs`, etc.) and wants specific real changes. IMPORTANT: four other background agents are concurrently working on NxLabs right now (GitHub import, Thunderstore import, Steam Workshop integration, and a hero/detail-page/description redesign). Before you start: run `git status` and `git log --oneline -5` to see what's already landed, `git pull` if needed, and scope your work ONLY to the mod card component — do not touch import scripts, `worker/game-mods.ts`, hero sections on `/mods` or `/dashboard/nxlabs` homepages, or mod DETAIL page headers (`[family]/[slug]/page.tsx` files) — another agent owns those. If you find file conflicts from a concurrent commit, re-read the current state and adapt rather than overwriting blindly.

## The component
`components/mods/ModCard.tsx` (and how it's rendered from `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx` — read both in full, plus `components/mods/GameBadge.tsx` since the current small game-icon badge likely lives there or is composed alongside the card).

## Real screenshot of current state (owner's exact words + what's visible)
A card showing: a "FEATURED" badge top-left, a large icon/image area with a generic letter-avatar ("C") since this particular mod (Rust's "Clans" plugin) has no real icon image, a tiny game-icon badge in the bottom-left corner of the image area (a small square Rust logo, described by the owner as "so small you can't even see it"), then below: category breadcrumb ("RUST · CLANS & SOCIAL"), mod name ("Clans"), description ("Clan creation, tags, roster and friendly-fire."), and below/outside the card a plain text line "No matching server yet — order one." with "order one" as a plain link.

## Requested changes (verbatim from the owner, your job is to execute these well)

1. **"No matching server yet" text** — currently sits as plain link text below/outside the card. Move it to the BOTTOM of the card itself (inside the card's boundary, as its own footer row), make it more concise (e.g. "No matching server" or similar short label), and turn the action into a real button (not a plain underlined link) — e.g. an "Order server" button. Check `QuickAddButton.tsx` for how the EXISTING "eligible server, one-click install" case renders its button, so the "no server yet" case gets a visually consistent sibling treatment (same footer row, different label/action) rather than a completely different look.

2. **Add a download button + total downloads count to the card.** Real data — `GameMod.downloads` already exists and is populated for sourced mods (check `formatDownloads` in `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, already used elsewhere). Add this as a real visible stat on the card (e.g. near the footer row, an icon + formatted count), and a real download action/button — check how the mod DETAIL page currently exposes its "Download"/"View on {source}" action (seen in a recent screenshot: a button labeled "View on GitHub" for GitHub-sourced mods) and reuse the same real link-resolution logic at the card level (don't invent a new download mechanism — reuse whatever the detail page already calls, likely `AddToServerWidget.tsx` or a shared resolver) so the card's download button goes to the same real, correct destination as the detail page's, per-source (GitHub release, Modrinth CDN, Thunderstore package, etc.).

3. **Replace the tiny game-icon badge with the game's real cover/box art, portrait aspect ratio, with a color-matched border.** Real assets already exist: `public/games/art/<slug>_poster.jpg` (see `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG[family].poster` for the exact slug mapping per family — do NOT assume the poster filename matches the gameFamily key directly, some differ, e.g. ark→"ark-asa", sdtd→"7-days-to-die" — read the real mapping). Use this real poster image (already portrait-oriented box art) in the badge position, sized large enough to actually read (the owner's complaint is specifically that the current one is unreadably small), in a corner of the card's image area matching current placement. For "a border matching the color of the game cover" — do NOT hand-pick arbitrary hex values; compute a real representative color from the actual poster image file (check if `sharp` is already a dependency — it's commonly used for image processing in Next.js projects — and if so use its `.stats()` or a simple average-color/dominant-color extraction at build/render time; a small, well-known color-extraction approach is fine, but the color must be genuinely derived from the real image, not guessed). If per-family average colors would be expensive to compute on every request, compute them once (e.g. a small build-time/cached lookup keyed by family) rather than recomputing per card render.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read `components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`, `components/mods/GameBadge.tsx`, `components/mods/QuickAddButton.tsx`, `components/mods/AddToServerWidget.tsx`, and `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG` in full before writing code.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Real Playwright before/after screenshots of the card in a few different real states (featured mod with real icon, a mod with no icon/letter-avatar fallback, a mod with an eligible server vs. one with none) to confirm all three changes render correctly and the layout doesn't break at different card-grid widths.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (never build directly in /opt/nxeon), verify staging HTTP 200 + visually correct, then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, confirm BUILD_ID changed + fresh service ActiveEnterTimestamp.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit with a clear message; confirm it reached `origin/main`. Check for conflicts with the other concurrent agents' commits before and after — rebase/re-pull if origin/main moved during your work.

Report back: confirmation all three changes are live with real screenshots described, and how you derived the poster border color (method used, whether computed live or cached).

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

  grid doesn't need a second per-mod query (`queryCatalogMods` already loads the full `GameMod` row
